question: In which of the following years did the Swadeshi movement take place to oppose the partition of Bengal?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1905**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Swadeshi movement took place in 1905 **to protest the British partition of Bengal
 
• The **Swadeshi movement was formally proclaimed on August 7, 1905, at the Calcutta Town Hall. **
 
• The movement was a protest against the British decision to partition Bengal, and involved boycotting British products and using Indian-made goods instead. 
 
• On **October 16, 1905, the day the partition came into effect, people in Calcutta called a hartal,** fasted, and paraded the streets singing "Bande Mataram". 
 
• **Key figures in the movement included Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Lala Lajpat Rai. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Timeline of Swadeshi movement:

 
 
• ​In 1900, Bengal was the major province in British India.
 
• The Indian national movement began in Bengal and thus, Britishers decided to part Bengal.
 
• When Lord Curzon, then Viceroy of India, announced the partition of Bengal in July 1905.
 
• Indian National Congress, initiated the Swadeshi movement in Bengal.
 
• Swadeshi movement was launched as a protest movement which also gave a lead to the Boycott movement in the country.
 
• In 1909, the movement had spread across the country and people had started anti-partition and anti-colonial movements.
 
• In Andhra Pradesh, the Swadeshi movement was also known as the Vandemataram movement In 1910.
 
• There were many secret associations that had been set up and there were many revolutionary movements, which were synonymous with the Swadeshi movement.
 
• Later movements by Mahatma Gandhi from 1915, such as the Satyagraha movement, the Non-Cooperation movement were based on the Swadeshi movement.
